title: As asked (B): proxy guard, description/below route, and seals at create and first dispatch
description:
Piece B of LIN-4345's approved plan (revision 2). **Blocked by piece A** (LIN-4345's read side: `lib/as-asked.js`, the reader rule, the brief composer). B uses A's module, and it must not seal any ticket until the readers are correct. Once B lands, the words are fixed and quoted, and the old prompts still work: a close-out that tries to rewrite the block gets a 422 telling it what to do instead.

## This piece's slice of the plan (implemented; pruned at close-out)

Plan steps 3–6 were implemented as approved, with all five builder notes from the approving verdict, in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2346](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2346>) (squash `d81e13e7`, deployed 7 Nov 2026):

* the proxy guard (422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE`);
* `POST …/description/below` (422 `NO_AS_ASKED_BLOCK`);
* the seals at create (proxy, session, feedback);
* the first-dispatch seal in `createDispatchItem`, through each lane's `sealAccess`, checked by an entrance census.

There is one deviation, which builder note 5 allows: Jira is skipped at create and at first dispatch, because the ADF round trip cannot hold the end line. The follow-up is LIN-4355.

The full step-by-step slice is preserved in this task's snapshots and in the comment trail. The close-out comment records the ledger and the post-deploy checks.

## Testing: witnesses 3, 4 and 5 (each must fail before the change)

* **Witness 3: no step can alter the words.** Run on LocalStore through the real proxy routes.
  * PATCH, and a replace that changes one character inside the block, get 422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE`. The message names the line, and the stored description is unchanged.
  * Append, replace below the block, and `description/below` succeed, and the block's bytes are unchanged.
  * `description/below` on an unsealed ticket gets `NO_AS_ASKED_BLOCK`.
  * A PATCH that adds a block, and a proxy create carrying a marker, are refused.
  * A session-lane PATCH that edits the block succeeds.
  * All of these also run on a Linear-style backslash-escaped body. Run the guard against the Jira fake too.
* **Witness 4: sealing.**
  * Each create lane stores the text verbatim inside the block, and feedback's triage marker sits after the end line.
  * A dispatch on a fresh issue seals it on every lane that names one (session, proxy, override, descent, kickoff). Run this on LocalStore, and show each lane failing before the change.
  * A second dispatch does not seal again. A feedback dispatch leaves its already-sealed ticket's bytes unchanged.
  * None of these seal: an issue whose only earlier row is in history; an issue with an earlier row still in the queue; an issue with no row whose description already holds `## Implementation Plan`; an empty description; an issue whose history read throws; a dispatch refused by the duplicate guard.
  * With no `sealAccess`, the row logs `seal skipped: no access` and is still enqueued. A failed or hung write leaves the row enqueued and logs it.
  * **Entrance census test:** every `createDispatchItem(` caller in `lib`/`routes` either passes `sealAccess` or is on the never-first list with its reason.
* **Witness 5: a whole ticket keeps the words.** Seed, dispatch (sealed), plan appends below, a close-out PATCH that drops the block (refused), a `description/below` prune (accepted). The filed words are still there at the end.

## Docs

* `docs/proxy-integration.md` documents the two 422 codes and `description/below`.
* `lib/proxy-instructions.js`: the PATCH, replace and below entries name the refusal.

## Acceptance

* Witnesses 3 to 5 pass and are shown failing before the change.
* The census test passes. `npm test` is green.
* The PR names any Jira gap as a ledger item, and lists the known, accepted mis-seal cases (likeliest break 2).

---

**Session fit:** fits one session

**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4345's approving plan-review (comment 23006cda-4b9f-4268-9392-a82d804ea7dd, rev 2)

**Grounding commit:** `e63c2f69` (main, 7 Nov 2026; the plan and all three plan-review verdicts were checked against it; main had not moved when this breakdown ran at 10:40 UTC)

**Starting point:** your starting point is the approved plan on the parent, LIN-4345 ("Every step reads what the person asked"). Read it in full under `## Implementation Plan` (revision 2) in LIN-4345's description, and read the approving verdict (comment 23006cda, 10:36 UTC on LIN-4345), including its "Notes for the builder". Follow the plan. Where the code shows the plan is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4345. The person's own words and the "Done looks like" are at the top of LIN-4345's description. Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

## Piece A has landed, and two checks wait for this piece's first live seal

LIN-4351 (piece A) merged as `fdd57fe9` (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345) and is deployed. It is Done, so this ticket is no longer blocked.

Review left two checks in LIN-4351's ledger that can only run once a ticket really carries an `## As asked` block, which only this piece can write. They were recorded on LIN-4351 as **not run**. Please run them on the first ticket B seals in production, and record the result in this ticket's close-out:

1. **Linear storage.** GET the sealed issue through the proxy.
   - Assert that `splitAsAsked(description)` (`lib/as-asked.js`) is non-null, and that its `words` equal the filed body when compared after `normalizeEscaping`.
   - A null result means every reader silently falls back to reading the whole description.
2. **The brief does not restate the block.** GET that ticket's brief (`/api/proxy/brief/<id>`, forcing a regeneration if needed).
   - Confirm the block's words appear once, as the quote at the top.
   - Confirm the model's four sections follow, and that they do not paraphrase the ask.

Rollback for piece A, as named by review: revert squash commit `fdd57fe9`.

## Piece B is built: PR open, CI green, waiting for review

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2346. Head is `36a59f5e5d343fb3b51128437bf5aebce69e6a68`. It is not merged; merging follows an independent review.

**CI:** green on that head (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42375184100). Unit tests, all four E2E shards and the secret scan passed, with no retries.
- The first run (42374342068, at `a8c823d2`) was red on E2E shard 4. In `task-page.spec.js`, the spec's own anchor dispatch was the seeded ticket's first dispatch, so the new seal wrapped the description and the page changed.
- The seal behaved as designed, but the spec depended on test order. It now seeds its tickets already sealed (`36a59f5e`).

**Local `npm test`:** unit 24,089 of 24,089 pass. E2E: 2,003 passed and 1 failed, `live-console.spec.js:444`. That spec also fails on main (`fdd57fe9`), so the failing-test names match on branch and main.

**What landed** (plan steps 3–6, all five builder notes from the approving verdict):
- **The guard:** the proxy's description writes return 422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE` if they would change, drop or forge the block.
- **The new route:** `POST …/description/below`, with 422 `NO_AS_ASKED_BLOCK` on a ticket that has no block.
- **Seals at create:** proxy, session and feedback creates file the description sealed.
- **The first-dispatch seal:** in `createDispatchItem`, through each lane's own `sealAccess`, checked by an entrance census test.

Witnesses 3, 4 and 5 are each shown failing before the change; the evidence is in the PR.

**Unguarded lanes, by design:** the session lane (PATCH and the task-edit page), edits made directly in Linear or GitHub, and agents that write to the provider without the proxy.

**Review ledger:**
1. **Jira cannot hold the block.** The ADF round trip turns the end line into `_End of what was asked. …_`.
   - Jira is skipped at create and at first dispatch, with its own log line (`seal skipped: provider jira cannot hold the block`), and the text is never reformatted.
   - On Jira the guard has no block to protect.
   - The fix would change piece A's fixed shape, so it needs a decision.
2. **The description-target attachment path is not tested end to end.** LocalStore has no `uploadFile`; the path goes through the same `editDescription` check.
3. **Seal deadline:** the first-dispatch seal shares one ~3s deadline (`PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`).
4. **Known, accepted mis-seal cases** (likeliest break 2):
   - a ticket last dispatched before dispatch history was kept, whose description holds research or scoping text but no plan line, gets sealed;
   - a filing that happens to contain a session-fit phrase, plan heading or `plan-review due:` line is not sealed.
   Piece C's "no block, no prune" rule protects both.

**After deploy:** run LIN-4351's two live-seal checks on the first ticket sealed in production. Find it by the `[as-asked] sealed at first dispatch (<urlKey> <identifier>)` log line, or by a ticket created after deploy, then record the results in this ticket's close-out:
1. `splitAsAsked` is non-null and its words equal the filed body.
2. The brief quotes the block once, at the top, without paraphrasing it.

## Review — LIN-4352

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2346 at head `36a59f5e5d343fb3b51128437bf5aebce69e6a68` (base `fdd57fe9` = current main; mergeable). The PR is **open, not merged**. The distilled brief says "implemented and merged", which is wrong; the 13:11 comment is right.

CI: green on head `36a59f5e` (run 42375184100: unit, E2E 1–4, secret scan, CI success).

### Scope vs plan
The diff matches plan steps 3–6 and the places the description names, with no overrun:
- **Guard:** PATCH `description`, append, replace and the description-target attachment all go through `refusedByAsAsked`. PATCH makes one `issueDescription` read; `issueWriteGuard` was not grown.
- **Create:** the proxy create refuses a body that already holds a marker line.
- **New route:** `description/below`, registered in `SPEC`, the catalog and the inventory/backstop tests.
- **Create seals:** proxy, session and feedback. Feedback keeps the priority line and triage marker after the end line.
- **First-dispatch seal:** at 1.7 in `createDispatchItem`, after every refusal guard (stopped run, duplicate, run limit, budget, close-out, composed run) and before `finalizePrompt` and 7.6.
- **Store read:** `hasDispatchForIssue` reads queue and history over the indexed `{urlKey, issueIdentifier}` and fails closed. History is wired in `server.js:459`.
- **All five builder notes are present in code.** The descent arm keys the seal by the row's `terminalIdentifier`, and the lane test proves it seals TEST-2, not TEST-1.

**Class check:** every `updateIssue` and `createIssue` caller outside the providers was enumerated. The proxy's description writes are all guarded. The other writers are the session PATCH (unguarded by design, step 5), `workspace-api-run-evidence.js` (state only), and the seal itself. No proxy GraphQL passthrough exists. All four providers implement `issueDescription`, so the new PATCH read adds no `CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED` regression.

**Regression check:** recent history on the touched files includes LIN-4317/4313 (periodical mint: it passes no `sealAccess`, and the census exempts it with its reason) and LIN-947 (feedback triage marker "always last": still last, now below the block). Nothing re-applies a reverted change.

### Tests and mutation checks (re-run here)
The new and changed suites (`as-asked-*`, `issue-write-routes`, inventory, backstop, rulings-pins) give **256/256 pass** locally on the head. I removed each claimed path and re-ran `tests/unit/as-asked-*.test.js`:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Guard removed from `editDescription` | 2 fail |
| Guard removed from PATCH | 8 fail |
| Create marker refusal removed | 2 fail |
| Fail-closed branch removed | 1 fail |
| `carriesStageState` dropped | 3 fail |
| History not read | 2 fail |
| Seal call removed | 17 fail |
| Feedback `below` folded into block | 3 fail |
| Kickoff `sealAccess` removed | 2 fail (census) |
| `issueAccessOf` gives no seal | 6 fail |
| Seal read keyed by wrong id | 14 fail |
| `providerHoldsAsAsked` bypassed (Jira) | 4 fail |
| Session create seal removed | 4 fail |
| Remove only the `earlier.value === true` return | 0 fail. **Equivalent mutation**: the next branch still returns without sealing. Not a gap. |
| `sealAccessFrom.write` uses `issueIdentifier` instead of the `id` `read` returned | **0 fail.** The "keyed by the id the read returned" test wraps `write` at the factory seam, and LocalStore accepts either key, so builder note 1's second half has no witness at the `sealAccessFrom` layer. Fix for close-out below. |

All mutations were reverted.

Test level is right: witnesses 3–5 drive the real proxy, session and feedback routes on LocalStore, plus the Jira fake. Witness 5 is a whole-ticket flow.

### Fix for close-out (before merge)
1. **`tests/unit/as-asked-dispatch-seal.test.js`, builder note 1 at the `sealAccessFrom` layer.** Add a test that builds `sealAccessFrom(() => ({ provider: fake, token: 't' }))`, where:
   - `fake.issueDescription(token, 'TEST-9')` returns `{ id: 'uuid-9', description: 'words' }`;
   - `fake.updateIssue(token, id, …)` succeeds only when `id === 'uuid-9'`.

   Then `createDispatchItem` with `issueIdentifier: 'TEST-9'` and that `sealAccess` must log `sealed at first dispatch`. Confirm it goes red when `lib/as-asked-seal.js:146` passes `issueIdentifier` instead of `id ?? issueIdentifier`.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Linear seal round trip keeps the words.** **Inside** (step 6, first-dispatch seal, builder note 4).
  - The seal reads Linear's backslash-escaped `issueDescription` and writes `sealAsAsked(thatText)` back. CI only uses a Linear-style fixture on LocalStore, not Linear's real write/read.
  - **After the deploy:** on the first ticket that logs `[as-asked] sealed at first dispatch (<urlKey> <identifier>)` (or a ticket created through the proxy after deploy), GET it through the proxy.
  - Assert `splitAsAsked(description)` is non-null and its `words` equal the filed body after `normalizeEscaping`. A null result, or escapes that pile up (`\\_`), is the failure.
  - This is LIN-4351's check 1.
- **The brief quotes the block once and does not paraphrase it.** **Inside** (the parent's "every step reads what the person asked"; a claim B's seal makes real for the first time).
  - **After the deploy:** GET `/api/proxy/brief/<that id>`, regenerating it if needed.
  - Pass: the words appear exactly once, as the quote at the top, followed by the four sections.
  - This is LIN-4351's check 2.
- **The guard refuses on a real Linear ticket.** **Inside** (step 3).
  - **After the deploy:** on that same sealed Linear ticket, call `description/replace` changing one character inside the block. Expect 422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE` naming the line, and the description unchanged.
  - Then call `description/below` with `{ "body": "x" }`. Expect 200, and the block's bytes unchanged.
- **The description-target attachment path has no end-to-end test.** **Inside** (step 3 lists `editDescription` :485/:680).
  - The code (`routes/proxy-writes.js:777`) goes through `editDescription(again, appendBlock…)`, so it shares append's guard, which is tested and was mutation-checked.
  - **Before the merge:** confirm by reading that line. It holds at `36a59f5e`. No further check is needed, so this is **discharged by inspection**.
- **Seal deadline under real latency.** **Inside** (step 6, bounded by `PLAN_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`).
  - **Named monitor:** the log lines `[as-asked] seal timed out (write may still land)` and `[as-asked] seal failed: … timed out`. Only production latency shows how often the shared ~3s deadline is hit.
  - The hang test proves the dispatch still enqueues.
- **Jira cannot hold the block.** **Outside** (the fix changes piece A's end-line shape in `lib/as-asked.js`, a different decision).
  - Inside this ticket, builder note 5's allowed route was taken: skip with `seal skipped: provider jira cannot hold the block`, and never reformat. The Jira-fake tests cover that, so it is **discharged**.
  - **Close-out files a follow-up** (check it does not already exist): "Accept `_…_` as the As asked end line so Jira can hold the block". No ruling exists on LIN-4352 or LIN-4345 for it.
- **Known, accepted mis-seal cases** (pre-history tickets with research text get sealed; filings containing a plan phrase stay unsealed). **Inside**, and accepted by the plan as likeliest break 2. Piece C's "no block, no prune" is the mitigation. **Discharged** as accepted risk.
- **`live-console.spec.js:444` fails locally on main and on the branch.** **Outside**. It is not in CI's failure set. Close-out may file it if no ticket exists.
- **Named rollback:** revert the squash commit of PR #2346. This removes the guard, the route and the seals.
  - Descriptions already sealed stay sealed. That is harmless: piece A's readers handle them, and the session lane can still edit them.
  - So the rollback is code-only, not data.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The work is complete against steps 3–6 and all five builder notes, and CI is green on `36a59f5e`. 14 of the 15 mutations on load-bearing paths go red; the fifteenth survives only because it is equivalent. Two things remain:
- **Before merge:** add the `sealAccessFrom` id-keying test above.
- **After deploy:** run the three live Linear checks above.

## Close-out — LIN-4352

**What merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2346, squash commit `d81e13e7deabef51900f032f07e09c7c8089cfae`. The merge was pinned with `--match-head-commit` to head `4b1cfa7015edfe10dad7008a49afc25b5958e6c1`. It covers plan steps 3–6 of LIN-4345: the proxy guard, `description/below`, the seals at create, and the first-dispatch seal.

**Deployed:** the harbour.cat footer showed `d81e13e7` at 13:36 UTC. All the post-deploy checks below ran against that deploy.

**Final CI:** green on `4b1cfa70`, run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42376378405. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, the secret scan and `CI success` all passed. I re-read the status immediately before merging.

### Changes made after the approval

| Commit | Change | Review line it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `4b1cfa70` | `tests/unit/as-asked-dispatch-seal.test.js` adds "sealAccessFrom writes by the id issueDescription returned, not the identifier". It uses a fake provider whose `issueDescription('TEST-9')` returns `{ id: 'uuid-9' }`, and whose `updateIssue` succeeds only when given `uuid-9`. | "Fix for close-out (before merge) 1: builder note 1 at the `sealAccessFrom` layer" |

**Mutation check, run here:** I changed `lib/as-asked-seal.js:146` to pass `issueIdentifier` instead of `id ?? issueIdentifier`. The new test went red (pass 0, fail 1); reverted, it is green again. On the new head, the `as-asked-*` suites pass 108/108 and the full `npm run test:unit` passes 24,090/24,090.

### Ledger: how each item was settled

1. **Linear seal round trip keeps the words** (inside, after the deploy). **Ran on LIN-4357,** a ticket I created through the proxy after the deploy. Its body held `**bold**`, a code span, `_underscore_`, `#`, `[brackets]`, `-` list items and a `*`. It was sealed at create.
   - `splitAsAsked(description)` is **non-null**, and the escapes did **not** pile up (no `\\`). Those are the two failures review named.
   - The strict assertion "words equal the filed body after `normalizeEscaping`" was **not** exactly true. Linear stores markdown in its own canonical form: `_underscore_` became `*underscore*`, and `- ` list markers became `* `.
     - Linear does this to every description, sealed or not: LIN-4355 was filed before the deploy, unsealed, and its `- ` bullets came back as `* `.
     - The rendered words are the same. Harbour wrote the body verbatim and did not reformat it.
     - The canonical form is stable once stored. After a `description/below` write, the block's bytes and `words` were identical to the first read.
   - **What this means:** a writer that rebuilds the block from the original filing text instead of the live description would get a false 422 if the filing used `_…_` or `-` bullets. That refusal is the safe direction; nothing leaks through. I am noting it here and filing nothing.
2. **The brief quotes the block once and does not paraphrase it** (inside, after the deploy). **Ran:** I force-regenerated the brief with `POST /api/proxy/brief/LIN-4357` (gpt-5.4-mini, 13:37 UTC).
   - The block is quoted verbatim exactly once, at the top, and the four sections follow. The block's long phrases appear once each. That meets review's stated pass criterion.
   - **Observation:** the test ticket has nothing but the ask, so the model's sections refer to it. They quote one 7-word phrase ("safe to ignore; cancelled by the close-out") twice, and one Constraints bullet describes the ask's formatting request. The brief prompt already forbids restating the block (`lib/brief.js:45`). I passed this evidence to LIN-4353, which owns the brief-model decision.
3. **The guard refuses on a real Linear ticket** (inside, after the deploy). **Ran on LIN-4357: pass.**
   - `description/replace` changing "first item" to "first iten" got 422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE`, naming block line 5. The description's sha256 was unchanged.
   - A PATCH that dropped the block got 422 `AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE` with kind `removed`.
   - `description/below {"body":"x"}` got 200, and the block's bytes were unchanged.
4. **The description-target attachment path** (inside). **Discharged by inspection,** re-confirmed at the merged code: `routes/proxy-writes.js:777` calls `editDescription(again, (existing) => appendBlock(existing, embedded))`, so it shares append's guard.
5. **Seal deadline under real latency** (inside). **Named monitor, as review wrote it:** the log lines `[as-asked] seal timed out (write may still land)` and `[as-asked] seal failed: … timed out`.
6. **Jira cannot hold the block** (outside). The skip-and-log path in this ticket is discharged by the Jira-fake tests. I found no existing ticket or ruling, so I filed **LIN-4355**, "Accept `_…_` as the As asked end line so Jira can hold the block" (Medium; Improvement, kind:follow-up, front:providers; related to LIN-4352).
7. **Known, accepted mis-seal cases** (inside). **Accepted risk** under the plan's "likeliest break 2"; piece C's "no block, no prune" rule mitigates it.
8. **`live-console.spec.js:444` fails locally** (outside). I reproduced it on this Mac. The failing test is "route A: .lc-pulse geometry… (LIN-1741)": its mobile width pin expects 319 and gets 334, the 15px scrollbar gutter that macOS overlay scrollbars do not reserve. I found no existing ticket, so I filed **LIN-4356** (Low; Bug, kind:follow-up, front:maintenance; related to LIN-4352 and LIN-1741).
9. **Named rollback, as review wrote it:** revert squash commit `d81e13e7`. This is code-only; already-sealed descriptions stay sealed, which is harmless.

**First-dispatch seal in production:** I saw no `[as-asked] sealed at first dispatch` log line during this session. Review allowed a ticket created through the proxy after deploy as the check subject, and LIN-4357 is that ticket. The first-dispatch path writes back the Linear-canonical text it reads, which item 1 shows is stable.

### Related tickets
- **LIN-4357** (the verification ticket) is cancelled; its purpose is recorded here.
- **LIN-4353** (piece C) is no longer blocked by this ticket. I left a note there with the brief observation.
- **LIN-4345** (the parent) stays In Progress until piece C lands.

## Autopilot run summary (stepper): LIN-4352

LIN-4352 is merged, deployed and Done. Every stage ran on opus (`anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`), as the human asked.

**Beats.** One warm implementation session, `3fa19d61`, did the work in four beats. Each beat's tests were shown failing before the change and passing after.
1. **Proxy guard and `description/below`** (`765fc447`). The witness-3 tests failed 18 of 27 before the change and pass 27 of 27 after. This beat also found that Jira's format conversion drops the block.
2. **Seals at create** (`3ec16e15`). The new tests failed 12 of 13 before and pass 13 of 13 after. All sealing lanes share one helper, `sealForFiling`, which checks whether the provider's conversion keeps the block.
3. **Seal at first dispatch and the entry-point census** (`717a2ecb`). There are 28 tests. Each dispatch lane failed before its wiring was added, and each mutation broke only its own cases.
4. **Witness 5, PR #2346 and CI.** The first CI run was red because a task-page E2E test's own dispatch was its ticket's first, so the seal wrapped the description it checked. That was fixed in `36a59f5e`, and CI went green on that commit.

**Review** (`33d42df9`, comment eaccf00d): Approve, on condition that close-out add a test that the seal writes by the id its read returned.

**Close-out** (`27ac7537`):
- It added that test in `4b1cfa70`, and the test failed when the write used the ticket identifier.
- PR #2346 merged as squash `d81e13e7`. CI run 42376378405 is green on head `4b1cfa70`, and the merged commit's checks are green too.
- The deploy landed at 13:36 UTC.
- The live checks ran on throwaway ticket LIN-4357, now Cancelled.
- It filed LIN-4355 (Jira's end line) and LIN-4356 (macOS live-console E2E), and pruned the description after archiving it.

**What I checked myself:** the PR is MERGED, its merge commit is `d81e13e7`, both check sets are green, LIN-4352 is Done, and LIN-4355, LIN-4356 and LIN-4357 exist in the states above.

**Still open:**
- **The seal at first dispatch hasn't been seen live yet.** The live check only exercised the seal at create. The `sealed at first dispatch` log line will identify the first one.
- **Linear rewrites some markdown when it stores a description**, for example `_x_` to `*x*`. A step that rebuilds the block from the original filing text, rather than the live description, would be refused. That fails safe.
- **The brief model still echoes the ask in its own sections.** That has been passed to LIN-4353.
- **LIN-4353 (piece C)** is now unblocked. It belongs to LIN-4345's next run, not this one.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** The guard and `description/below` were easy: piece A's `checkAsAsked` did the work. The difficulty bound in `createDispatchItem` and the six lanes feeding it, each holding its provider and token differently:
- session builds one from `ctx` or the call scope;
- the proxy lanes use `credentialFor`;
- kickoff dropped its token after the context read;
- feedback had one only inside the route.

I added a provider write to the dispatch path without disturbing the guard order, the mint or the pilot window, in a file the census tests read as text. Testing every lane on LocalStore meant test-token mode with an injected LocalProvider, because descent needs a model call. Two surprises cost the most:
- Jira's ADF round trip turns the end line into `_End…_`.
- The E2E dispatch store survives between specs, so whether a seal happened depended on test order.

**2. What I'd have done first.** Run one sealed body through every provider's round trip, before any code. The Jira result decides whether the end marker should accept either emphasis form, which is piece A's call.

**3. What I'd tidy.**
- In test-token E2E workspaces the seal sends a real Linear read and gets a 401. It should skip the test sentinel, as the plan reads do.
- Three small access adapters (`sealAccessFrom`, `issueAccessOf`, `proxyAccess`) should become one lane-access object on `run`.
- Seal outcomes are console strings; a structured event would make the first live seals queryable.

**4. If this area were how I'd want it.** Each lane would resolve one `issueAccess { provider, token }` once, on `run`, for the referent guard, plan read, title read and seal. The end marker wouldn't depend on emphasis. This ticket would then have been "add a seal step to the factory that reads `run.issueAccess`": no per-lane plumbing, no Jira gap.

**5. What the ticket and plan got wrong.**
- The session create was at :748, not :796.
- "LocalStore for every store backend": LocalStore holds issues; the dispatch store is one class.
- A create seal on Jira can't happen: Jira has no `createIssue`.
- Kickoff has no `readPlanBlock` to share a helper with.
- Jira was treated as a guard re-escaping risk; the real break is the marker's shape.

**6. What it left behind.**
- `lib/as-asked-seal.js` beside `lib/as-asked.js`: two modules for one concept.
- `descriptionRoundTrip`, an off-surface provider method only Jira implements, declared nowhere in the interface.
- `carriesStageState` repeats patterns that also live in each reader.
- A new store method, `hasDispatchForIssue`.
- The credential is now read for the referent guard, the plan read and the seal; `issueAccessOf` unifies only the last two.
- Simpler: close-out can prune through `description/below` without re-sending anything, which piece C needs.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** Yes. The guard protects nothing until blocks exist, and seals are unsafe without the guard; witness 5 only means something with both. Split across tickets, each half would have proved nothing. The four beats gave the session boundaries. My line: B1 = guard, `below`, create seals; B2 = first-dispatch seal and census, which carried most of the risk.
